boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Kalamazoo College traditions, from a secretly scheduled spring day off to student-run performances and ceremonial objects.

cards.title: Wait for the Bells to Cancel Class
cards.subtitle: A secretly scheduled spring day off known as DOGL
cards.notes: Listen for the chapel bells during spring term, then follow the College’s current transportation and event guidance for the day.
cards.short_summary: A surprise day without classes sends the K community toward Lake Michigan and campus activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College says DOGL began in 1974, occurs on a secretly selected spring date, cancels classes and includes College-provided transportation to South Haven.
cards.source_title: Day of Gracious Living | About Kalamazoo College
cards.access_notes: The date is intentionally unannounced in advance; students should rely on current College communications when the bells signal DOGL.

cards.title: Play Casino Games with the President
cards.subtitle: K’s themed casino night in Hicks Student Center
cards.notes: Dress for the year’s theme, take photos and play the event’s casino-style games; confirm the current student schedule before attending.
cards.short_summary: Hicks becomes a themed casino floor staffed by faculty, staff and even the College president.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College identifies Monte Carlo as a continuing tradition first celebrated in 1975, with themed décor and casino tables staffed by faculty and staff, including the president.
cards.access_notes: Held as a campus student event in Hicks Student Center; check current Office of Student Involvement announcements for timing and entry details.

cards.title: See Hicks Turn into a Cultural Stage
cards.subtitle: An annual collaboration among multicultural student groups
cards.notes: Arrive ready for student performances and cultural presentations; use the current event listing for date, location and attendance details.
cards.short_summary: Multiple student organizations combine performances and international food in one campus-wide celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: The College describes Afro Fiesta Desi Sol as an annual event where multicultural student organizations transform Hicks Student Center with performances and international food.
cards.source_title: Diversity at Kalamazoo College - Life at K
cards.access_notes: An annual campus tradition; programming and entry arrangements can change, so consult the College’s current event calendar.

cards.title: Watch a Night Market Take the Stage
cards.subtitle: An annual event organized by Asian and Pacific Islander groups
cards.notes: Look for the annual program of music, dance, poetry and fashion, and verify this year’s venue and attendance information before going.
cards.short_summary: Student groups assemble modern and traditional performance forms into K’s annual Night Market.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College documents Night Market as an annual event organized by Asian and Pacific Islander student groups and featuring music, dance, poetry and fashion.
cards.source_title: Diversity at Kalamazoo College - Life at K
cards.access_notes: Annual campus event with variable scheduling; confirm the current date, venue and audience requirements through College channels.

cards.title: Challenge Gender Norms at Pride Ball
cards.subtitle: Kaleidoscope’s annual celebration of queer culture
cards.notes: Wear clothing that feels right for you and check the current program for music, fashion and drag performances before heading to the event.
cards.short_summary: Kaleidoscope hosts a yearly party centered on queer culture, fashion, music and drag performance.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies Pride Ball as an annual party sponsored by Kaleidoscope that celebrates queer culture through music, fashion and drag performances.
cards.source_title: Diversity at Kalamazoo College - Life at K
cards.access_notes: Annual student event; consult current College or Kaleidoscope announcements for the date, venue and attendance rules.

cards.title: Catch Both Annual Frelon Shows
cards.subtitle: Student-led dance spanning ballet, Irish step and hip-hop
cards.notes: Watch for Frelon’s two yearly performance announcements, then confirm the venue and ticket or entry arrangements for the selected show.
cards.short_summary: K’s student dance company stages two annual showcases featuring markedly different movement traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College’s student-organization page states that Frelon Dance Company hosts two annual performances featuring styles from ballet and Irish step to hip-hop.
cards.source_title: Kalamazoo College Student Organizations — Life at K
cards.access_notes: Two performances are held annually; dates, venues and admission arrangements should be verified in current College event notices.

cards.title: Hear Eight Bells Speak for Campus
cards.subtitle: English change ringing from Stetson Chapel’s tower
cards.notes: Pause on campus when the bells mark a major occasion, and contact the College’s bell community before seeking any tower or ringing access.
cards.short_summary: Eight inscribed English bells announce moments such as graduation, reflections and DOGL.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says Stetson Chapel has eight English change-ringing bells that announce important events including community reflections, graduation and DOGL.
cards.access_notes: The bells can be heard across campus; tower access and hands-on ringing require authorization and should not be assumed.

cards.title: Return for a Reunion-Style Homecoming
cards.subtitle: A fall tradition dating to the first homecoming game in 1919
cards.notes: Build a weekend around the published athletics, concert, tour and reunion schedule; register wherever the current program requires it.
cards.short_summary: K’s homecoming now mixes Hornet athletics with reunions, campus history and student-alumni events.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College traces its first homecoming game to 1919 and describes today’s homecoming as a reunion weekend involving athletics and alumni-campus programming.
cards.access_notes: Homecoming programming varies by year; use the official weekend schedule for registration, venue and audience information.

cards.title: Follow a President’s Gold-Tipped Walking Stick
cards.subtitle: The College mace leads formal academic processions
cards.notes: Watch the head of a formal academic procession for the chief faculty marshal carrying the gold-tipped stick presented in 1859.
cards.short_summary: A former president’s walking stick became the ceremonial object leading K’s academic processions.
cards.evidence_claim: The College states that students gave the gold-tipped stick to first president James A. B. Stone in 1859 and that it is traditionally carried by the chief faculty marshal in academic processions.
cards.source_title: Stone Walking Stick | About Kalamazoo College
cards.access_notes: Visible during applicable formal academic processions; participation and seating depend on the rules for the specific ceremony.

cards.title: Enter K by Joining Its Honor System
cards.subtitle: A written commitment expected from incoming students
cards.notes: Read the Honor System before completing the written commitment, and ask the Dean of Students when a rule or responsibility is unclear.
cards.short_summary: Joining the College includes formally accepting shared responsibility for its academic community.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College says all entering students are expected to understand and follow its Honor System and indicate their willingness to do so in writing.
cards.source_title: About the Honor System – For Parents and Families | Kalamazoo College
cards.access_notes: This is an entering-student commitment rather than a public event; follow the College’s official onboarding process.
